original_test_intent: Obtain and validate the platform thermal-limit policy from the intended BMC over an authenticated remote path once the exact object, command, response semantics and acceptance policy are defined.
original_method: Preserve the TBD source and prohibit execution; require an authoritative OOB read contract plus immutable endpoint and secret-safe session controls before a bounded query is created.
manual_activity: The spec owner defines the thermal object, exact remote read, selector, schema, units and expected policy; the network/platform owner approves the BMC endpoint, cipher and secret delivery, and confirms the finalized procedure before execution.
required_inputs: Vendor DCMI/BMC thermal-limit application note or corrected testcase
Exact OOB read command and selector
BMC endpoint bound to immutable SUT identity
Approved cipher and secret-safe credential source
safety_requirements: Do not guess an OOB command
Do not infer from power-limit cases
Keep credentials out of argv and evidence
No thermal setter, fan, throttle, power or reset action
agent_execution_scope: Define thermal object, OOB command and decoder
Validate secret-safe session and no-mutation semantics
Run one bounded read after approval
engineer_actions: Supply and approve specification, remote target and acceptance oracle

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: No executable command is provided, appropriately reflecting the TBD source; the absence of an OOB route, selector, identity proof and credential contract must be resolved rather than filled from neighboring cases.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Do not run a command now. After an authoritative artifact defines the exact OOB thermal-limit read, execute it once over an identity-bound, secret-safe session, validate every response field and compare with the approved policy.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The source's OOB title and 10/5 timing remain; no endpoint, cipher, opcode, selector, unit or expected value is inferred.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Turn the placeholder into a remotely attributable read contract: define the thermal object and protocol, bind the BMC to the SUT, protect credentials, establish the policy oracle and then perform one redacted read.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds a safe resolution path for both missing semantics and missing OOB identity/session controls.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: The IB sibling does not establish LANPlus or remote attribution, and DCMI power-limit commands do not establish the thermal object.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: A guessed remote request can reach the wrong controller or an unintended state-changing command; plausible returned bytes have no meaning without target, schema and units.

project_override_considerations: A Redfish/vendor API is acceptable only after mapping the same thermal object, target scope, units and policy while preserving endpoint identity; omitted LANPlus/raw coverage must be disclosed.
expected_evidence: Defined thermal object, remote command, selector and response schema
Units/scaling, firmware support and approved expected policy
Immutable SUT/BMC endpoint and redacted secret-safe session
After approval: exact request, full response, completion and decoded fields
No secret leakage or thermal/power/configuration/log mutation

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The title identifies an OOB thermal-limit getter while Procedure and Criteria are placeholders. The row is incomplete but does not assert two contradictory operations.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The read purpose and remote route are identifiable. A vendor/corrected artifact, endpoint and access contract are concrete prerequisites; BLOCKED applies only if those still leave semantics, scope or acceptance irreducibly uncertain.

review_improvement: Defines how a non-runnable OOB placeholder can become a target-bound, secret-safe thermal-policy read without guessing protocol details.
independent_technical_reasoning: The thermal object cannot be inferred from adjacent power policy, and the remote transport adds an orthogonal identity problem: a reachable BMC is not proof of the intended server. Before execution, an authoritative artifact must bind the title to a precise read and decoder, while immutable endpoint evidence must bind that read to hardware. Until both are present, even a read-only-looking byte sequence is unsafe to interpret or execute.
